name: AML Screening Process

context: Audience | Financial Crime Staff, Compliance, Branch Staff

name: Head of Financial Crime
description: Senior leadership role responsible for ownership and governance of the AML Screening SOP at FirstUK Bank.

name: Financial Crime Staff
description: Operational team responsible for executing AML screening procedures and controls as defined in the SOP.
context: Audience | Financial Crime Staff, Compliance, Branch Staff

name: Compliance Staff
description: Compliance personnel responsible for oversight and validation of AML screening procedures.
context: Audience | Financial Crime Staff, Compliance, Branch Staff

name: Branch Staff
description: Front-line branch personnel who support AML screening procedures and customer interactions.
context: Audience | Financial Crime Staff, Compliance, Branch Staff

name: AML Screening Compliance Checkpoint
description: Mandatory regulatory gate requiring verification of AML screening obligations before customer onboarding or transaction processing proceeds. Governed by FirstUK Bank's AML policy and customer identification procedures.

name: AML Screening Process

systematic screening of customers against regulatory lists

systematic screening of customers against regulatory lists

name: PEP Screening

context: detect and prevent money laundering, terrorist financing, and sanctions violations
systematic screening of customers against regulatory lists

name: Customer
description: Natural person subject to AML screening procedures. Customers are systematically screened against regulatory lists to detect and prevent money laundering and sanctions violations.
context: systematic screening of customers against regulatory lists
detect and prevent money laundering, terrorist financing, and sanctions violations

name: Sanctions Compliance Checkpoint
description: Mandatory regulatory gate verifying that customers and transactions have been screened against sanctions lists before proceeding. Ensures compliance with sanctions regulations as part of AML obligations.
context: detect and prevent money laundering, terrorist financing, and sanctions violations
systematic screening of customers against regulatory lists

name: PEP Identification Compliance Checkpoint
description: Mandatory regulatory gate verifying identification and flagging of politically exposed persons. Ensures compliance with enhanced due diligence requirements for high-risk customer categories.
context: detect and prevent money laundering, terrorist financing, and sanctions violations
systematic screening of customers against regulatory lists

name: Terrorist Financing Prevention Compliance Checkpoint
description: Mandatory regulatory gate to prevent terrorist financing through systematic screening of customers and transactions. Ensures compliance with counter-terrorism financing regulations.
context: detect and prevent money laundering, terrorist financing, and sanctions violations
systematic screening of customers against regulatory lists

name: Customer Account Opening Process
description: End-to-end procedure for opening new customer accounts, applicable to all new account openings on a mandatory basis. The process encompasses identity verification, address verification, AML screening, and compliance checkpoint validation before account activation.
context: Applies to: All new customer account openings (mandatory)

name: Periodic Customer Re-screening Process
description: Recurring AML and compliance re-screening procedure applied to existing customers at defined intervals based on risk classification. High-risk customers are re-screened quarterly, while standard-risk customers are re-screened annually.
context: Periodic re-screening (high-risk customers quarterly, standard annually)

name: Transaction Monitoring Process
description: Continuous automated monitoring of customer transactions to detect suspicious activity patterns and potential money laundering indicators. This process operates on an ongoing basis across all monitored accounts.

name: Suspicious Activity Assessment and Reporting Process
description: Procedure for assessing suspicious activity identified through transaction monitoring or customer screening, determining whether a Suspicious Activity Report (SAR) must be filed with the relevant authority, and managing the reporting obligation.
context: Applies to: All new customer account openings (mandatory)

name: Identity Verification
description: Mandatory compliance control to verify the identity of new customers during account opening. This verification is a prerequisite for account activation and is part of the broader Know Your Customer obligation.

name: Address Verification
description: Mandatory compliance control to verify the residential or business address of new customers during account opening. Address verification is a core component of KYC requirements for all new accounts.

name: Sanctions Screening
description: Mandatory AML control screening new and existing customers against sanctions lists and Politically Exposed Person (PEP) databases. Applied at account opening and during periodic re-screening cycles.
context: Periodic re-screening (high-risk customers quarterly, standard annually)

name: Ongoing Transaction Monitoring
description: Automated, continuous monitoring of customer transactions to identify suspicious patterns, high-value transfers, and potential money laundering activity. Operates on an ongoing basis across all customer accounts.

name: New Customer
description: Individual applying for or opening a new account with the bank. Subject to mandatory KYC verification, AML screening, and compliance checkpoints before account activation.

name: High-Risk Customer
description: Existing customer classified as high-risk based on risk assessment criteria. Subject to enhanced due diligence, quarterly re-screening, and more frequent transaction monitoring review.
context: Periodic re-screening (high-risk customers quarterly, standard annually)

name: Standard-Risk Customer
description: Existing customer classified as standard-risk based on risk assessment criteria. Subject to annual re-screening and standard transaction monitoring procedures.
context: Periodic re-screening (high-risk customers quarterly, standard annually)

name: New Account
description: Customer account being opened for the first time. Must pass all mandatory compliance checkpoints including KYC verification, AML screening, and sanctions checks before activation.

name: New Account Opening Compliance Checkpoint
description: Mandatory regulatory gate that must be passed before a new account can be activated. Verifies completion of KYC verification, AML screening, sanctions checks, and all required due diligence documentation.

name: Periodic Re-screening Compliance Checkpoint
description: Mandatory regulatory gate for periodic customer re-screening. Verifies that high-risk customers are re-screened quarterly and standard-risk customers annually against current sanctions and PEP lists.
context: Periodic re-screening (high-risk customers quarterly, standard annually)

name: AML Screening Process
description: End-to-end anti-money laundering screening workflow triggered upon customer application receipt. The process includes automated list screening, match assessment, manual review escalation if hits are found, and results recording. Timeline ranges from under 5 minutes for automated screening to 1–24 hours for manual review of flagged matches.
context: Timeline: <5 minutes (automated), 1–24 hours (manual review if hit)

name: Initiate Screening
description: First step in the AML screening process where customer application data is prepared and screening is initiated against regulatory lists.

name: Screen Against Lists
description: Automated screening of customer data against sanctions, PEP, and other regulatory watchlists to identify potential matches.

name: Assess Match
description: Evaluation of screening results to determine whether a match has been identified against regulatory lists. This step branches the workflow based on match outcome.

name: Record Results
description: Documentation and recording of AML screening results in the system for audit and compliance purposes.

name: Hit Handling
description: Execution of defined procedures when a match (hit) is identified during screening, including manual review and escalation protocols.

name: Match Found Decision
description: Branching decision point following match assessment. If no match is found, screening proceeds to completion. If a match is found, the workflow escalates to manual review.

name: Sanctions and PEP List Screening
description: Automated and manual screening of customer application data against sanctions lists and Politically Exposed Person (PEP) registers as part of the AML screening process.

name: AML Screening Compliance Gate
description: Mandatory regulatory compliance gate that verifies completion of AML screening before customer application can proceed. Results must be recorded and any hits escalated for manual review.

name: Applicant Customer
description: The individual or entity submitting an application that triggers the AML screening process. The customer's data is screened against regulatory lists as part of onboarding compliance.

name: AML Screening Process
description: An end-to-end anti-money laundering screening procedure triggered automatically on new customer account opening, during periodic re-screening on a risk-based schedule, or manually upon compliance concern. The process captures customer information, prepares screening queries, and initiates checks against all configured lists.
context: Automatic Screening On: New customer account opening (before account creation)
Initiates screening against all configured lists

name: Initiate Screening
description: The first step in the AML screening process where compliance staff enters customer information into the screening system to prepare the screening query. This step captures all required customer data elements needed for screening.
context: Initiates screening against all configured lists

name: Screening Trigger Evaluation
description: The decision point that determines whether screening should be initiated based on three trigger conditions: new customer account opening, periodic re-screening on a risk-based schedule, or manual request due to compliance concern or unusual activity.
context: Automatic Screening On: New customer account opening (before account creation)

name: Customer Information Collection
description: The step where required customer data elements are gathered for screening purposes, including full legal name, date of birth, nationality, country of residence, and business name where applicable.

name: System Query Preparation and List Screening
description: The automated step where the screening system prepares the screening query from collected customer information and initiates screening checks against all configured lists.
context: Initiates screening against all configured lists

name: Compliance Staff
description: The operational role responsible for entering customer information into the screening system and initiating the AML screening process. Compliance staff execute the data entry and system query preparation steps.

name: Screening System
description: The automated system responsible for preparing screening queries from customer information and executing screening checks against all configured lists as part of the AML screening process.
context: Initiates screening against all configured lists

name: Sanctions and PEP List Screening
description: The AML screening execution that checks customer information against all configured lists, including sanctions lists and PEP (Politically Exposed Person) lists, as part of the account opening and periodic re-screening process.
context: Initiates screening against all configured lists
Automatic Screening On: New customer account opening (before account creation)

name: New Customer
description: A customer applying for or opening a new account who is subject to automatic AML screening before account creation. The customer's information is collected and screened against configured lists.
context: New customer account opening (before account creation)

name: Existing Customer
description: A customer with an existing account who is subject to periodic re-screening on a risk-based schedule as part of ongoing AML compliance obligations.

name: AML Screening Compliance Checkpoint
description: The mandatory regulatory compliance gate where customer information must be screened against configured sanctions and PEP lists before account creation or as part of periodic re-screening. The checkpoint verifies that AML screening obligations have been executed.
context: Automatic Screening On: New customer account opening (before account creation)
Initiates screening against all configured lists

name: Sanctions Screening Against Regulatory Lists
description: Mandatory compliance gate requiring screening of customers and entities against six regulatory sanctions and PEP lists maintained by US, EU, UK, and UN authorities. Any match against OFAC, EU, UK Treasury, or UN lists triggers immediate escalation; PEP matches trigger enhanced due diligence. Screening is continuous with daily or real-time updates.
context: PEP match = enhanced due diligence (not auto-block)

name: OFAC Sanctions List Screening
aliases: Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons
description: Screening against the US Treasury Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons list covering global individuals and entities under US sanctions. Updated daily with any match requiring immediate escalation.
context: Authority: US Treasury Office of Foreign Assets Control
List: Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons (SDN)

name: EU Consolidated Sanctions List Screening
description: Screening against the European Commission's EU Common Foreign & Security Policy sanctions list covering individuals and entities under EU sanctions. Updated daily with any match requiring immediate escalation.
context: List: EU Common Foreign & Security Policy sanctions

name: HM Treasury Sanctions List Screening
description: Screening against the UK Treasury (Office of Financial Sanctions Implementation, OFSI) sanctions designations list covering individuals and entities under UK sanctions. Updated daily with any match requiring immediate escalation.
context: Authority: UK Treasury (Office of Financial Sanctions Implementation, OFSI)

name: UN Sanctions List Screening
description: Screening against the UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions list covering global terrorism and other UN sanctions designations. Updated weekly with any match requiring immediate escalation.
context: List: Consolidated UN sanctions (terrorism, weapons, etc.)

name: Politically Exposed Persons Screening
description: Screening against third-party PEP databases (World-Check, Dow Jones, etc.) identifying current and former government officials, senior politicians, military personnel, their families, and close associates. Updated in real-time with matches triggering enhanced due diligence rather than automatic blocking.
context: Authority: Third-party data provider (World-Check, Dow Jones, etc.)
List: Politically Exposed Persons (government officials, senior politicians, military)
Hits: PEP match = enhanced due diligence (not auto-block)

name: Adverse Media Screening
description: Screening against news database aggregators to identify criminal convictions, fraud allegations, and sanctions violations from media sources. Updated daily with material adverse media matches requiring escalation for assessment.
context: List: Criminal convictions, fraud allegations, sanctions violations (from news)
Hits: Material adverse media = escalation for assessment

name: Sanctions List Match Decision
description: Binary decision gate triggered when customer screening against OFAC, EU, UK Treasury, or UN sanctions lists returns a match. Any positive match mandates immediate escalation; no alternative path exists.

name: PEP Match Decision
description: Decision gate triggered when customer screening against PEP databases returns a match. Unlike sanctions matches, PEP matches do not auto-block but instead trigger enhanced due diligence procedures for further assessment.
context: PEP match = enhanced due diligence (not auto-block)
Hits: PEP match = enhanced due diligence (not auto-block)

name: Adverse Media Assessment Decision
description: Decision gate triggered when adverse media screening identifies material negative news (criminal convictions, fraud allegations, sanctions violations). Material matches require escalation for assessment; immaterial mentions do not trigger action.
context: Material adverse media = escalation for assessment
Hits: Material adverse media = escalation for assessment

name: Screening Execution
description: An automated end-to-end process that executes sanctions and PEP list screening against customer records. The system searches configured screening lists, applies configurable match thresholds, and returns results within approximately one minute. Close matches and name variations are included in the screening scope.
context: System enters customer name into screening engine
Screening engine searches all configured lists
System checks for exact and close-match results

name: Customer Name Entry into Screening Engine
description: The initial step where the system enters the customer name into the screening engine to initiate the screening process.
context: System enters customer name into screening engine

name: Screening List Search
description: The screening engine searches all configured lists to identify potential matches against the customer name provided.
context: Screening engine searches all configured lists

name: Exact and Close-Match Results Check
description: The system evaluates screening results to identify both exact matches and close matches, including name variations and typos, against the configured match threshold.
context: System checks for exact and close-match results

name: Screening Results Return
description: The screening engine returns results to the system, typically within one minute, including matched names, the list source, and match scores.
context: Result includes: Matched name, list, match score

name: Screening Engine System
description: An automated system responsible for executing the screening process, searching configured lists, applying match thresholds, and returning screening results.
context: Screening engine searches all configured lists
System checks for exact and close-match results

name: Sanctions and PEP List Screening
description: An automated AML screening process that searches customer names against all configured sanctions and PEP lists. The screening applies configurable match thresholds (typically 80%+) and includes close matches based on name variations and typos.
context: Screening engine searches all configured lists

name: Screened Customer
description: A customer whose name, date of birth, and nationality are entered into the screening engine for AML compliance verification against configured sanctions and PEP lists.
context: System enters customer name into screening engine

name: Account Opening Process
description: End-to-end account opening workflow that includes KYC verification and AML screening. The process proceeds to account opening upon successful completion of screening with no matches against sanctions or watchlists.
context: Proceed with account opening (KYC already complete)

name: Assess Screening Results
description: Evaluation step that determines whether screening results show no matches across sanctions lists, watchlists, or adverse media. This assessment gates the decision to proceed with account opening.
context: Screening shows NO hits across all lists

name: Record Screening Passed Status
description: System recording step that documents the successful completion of screening checks. Includes recording the screening date and system reference for audit and compliance purposes.
context: Note screening date and system reference

name: Screening Results Gate
description: Binary compliance gate that branches based on screening results. No matches across all lists permits account opening to proceed; any match would trigger escalation or rejection.
context: Screening shows NO hits across all lists
Proceed with account opening (KYC already complete)

name: Sanctions and Watchlist Screening Checkpoint
description: Mandatory regulatory compliance gate verifying that the customer is not listed on any sanctions lists or watchlists. Screening must show no hits before account opening can proceed.
context: Screening shows NO hits across all lists

name: Adverse Media Screening Checkpoint
description: Mandatory regulatory compliance gate verifying that no adverse media has been identified against the customer. Clearance on this checkpoint is required before proceeding with account opening.
context: Screening shows NO hits across all lists

name: Know Your Customer Verification
description: KYC verification process that has already been completed prior to the screening assessment step. Completion of KYC is a prerequisite for proceeding to account opening upon successful screening.
context: Proceed with account opening (KYC already complete)

name: AML Screening
description: Anti-Money Laundering screening process that checks customer against sanctions lists, watchlists, and adverse media. Results determine whether account opening can proceed or requires escalation.
context: Screening shows NO hits across all lists

name: Account Applicant
description: Individual applying for account opening who is subject to KYC verification and AML screening. The customer must clear all compliance checkpoints before account opening is approved.
context: Proceed with account opening (KYC already complete)

name: Account Opening Process
description: The end-to-end account opening workflow that includes screening checks and compliance gates. The process is halted immediately upon detection of a potential match during screening, triggering escalation to the Financial Crime team for manual review.
context: Escalate to Financial Crime team for manual review

name: Screening Execution
description: The automated screening step that checks applicant details against watchlists and sanctions lists. The step produces a match score and identifies the matched name and list source.

name: Account Opening Halt
description: The immediate action taken upon detection of a screening match. The account opening process is stopped and no further progression occurs until manual review is completed.

name: Escalation to Financial Crime Team
description: The escalation step triggered by a screening match. The case is escalated to the Financial Crime team for manual investigation and determination of whether the match is a true positive or false positive.
context: Escalate to Financial Crime team for manual review

name: Match Details Documentation
description: The step where match details including match score, matched name, and list source are formally recorded in the system for audit and compliance purposes.

name: Manual Review Process Initiation
description: The formal initiation of manual review by the Financial Crime team following a screening match. This step begins the investigation to determine the validity and risk level of the match.

name: Financial Crime Team
description: The team responsible for receiving escalated screening matches and conducting manual review to determine whether a match represents a genuine compliance risk or a false positive.
context: Escalate to Financial Crime team for manual review

name: Screening Match Detection Gate
decision_question: Does screening show a potential match (HIT) against watchlists or sanctions lists?
path_yes: STOP account opening, escalate to Financial Crime team, document match details, initiate manual review
description: The critical compliance gate where screening results are evaluated. A positive match (HIT) triggers immediate halt of account opening and escalation to Financial Crime team.
context: Escalate to Financial Crime team for manual review

name: Sanctions and Watchlist Screening Checkpoint
regulatory_basis: Anti-Money Laundering and sanctions compliance requirements
evidence_required: Screening results with match score, matched name, and list source
description: The mandatory compliance checkpoint where applicants are screened against sanctions lists and watchlists during account opening. Results must be documented and any matches escalated for manual review.

name: Sanctions Screening
description: The automated AML screening process that checks applicant details against sanctions lists and watchlists, producing a match score and identifying any potential hits that require manual review.

name: Manual Review Process
description: A manual review workflow executed by Financial Crime Staff to assess sanctions/PEP screening matches. The process evaluates match quality, demographic alignment, and entity type to determine whether a hit represents a true positive requiring escalation, a false positive allowing clearance, or an uncertain case requiring deeper investigation.

name: Preliminary Assessment
description: The initial evaluation phase where Financial Crime Staff systematically review screening match characteristics including match score, name variance, date of birth alignment, nationality, and entity type classification.

name: Match Score Evaluation
description: Assessment of the numerical match score between the customer record and the sanctions/PEP list entry, with 80% or higher indicating a likely match requiring further consideration.
context: Match Score: How close is the match? (80%+ = likely match)

name: Name Variance Analysis
description: Examination of differences between the customer name and the matched list entry to distinguish between typographical errors, nicknames, or legitimate name variations versus exact matches.
context: Name Variance: Typo/nickname vs. exact match?

name: Date of Birth Verification
description: Comparison of the customer's date of birth against the matched list entry to determine alignment or significant discrepancies that may indicate a different person.
context: Date of Birth: Does DOB match or differ significantly?

name: Nationality Verification
description: Verification that the customer's nationality matches or differs from the matched list entry, used as a discriminating factor in hit assessment.

name: Entity Type Classification
description: Determination of whether the screening match is against an individual person or an organization, to assess relevance to the customer record being reviewed.
context: Business: Is match against individual or organization?

name: Hit Assessment Decision
description: A three-way branching decision point where Financial Crime Staff classify the screening match as a clear false positive, a likely true positive requiring escalation, or an uncertain case requiring deeper investigation based on preliminary assessment findings.

name: Clear False Positive Classification
description: Outcome path where the match is determined to be a false positive due to similar name but different person, allowing the customer to proceed without escalation.
context: A) Clear False Positive: Similar name but different person → Clear to proceed

name: Likely True Positive Classification
description: Outcome path where name, date of birth, and nationality all match the list entry, triggering immediate escalation of the case for compliance action.
context: B) Likely True Positive: Name, DOB, nationality all match → Escalate immediately

name: Uncertain Match Classification
description: Outcome path where the match shows partial alignment across demographic fields, requiring deeper investigation and research before a final determination can be made.
context: C) Uncertain: Partial match requiring investigation → Deeper research

name: Financial Crime Staff
description: The operational team responsible for executing the manual review process, evaluating screening matches against defined criteria, and making initial hit assessment decisions.

name: Sanctions and PEP List Screening
description: The automated or system-generated screening process that produces matches against sanctions and PEP lists, which are then subject to manual review and hit assessment by Financial Crime Staff.
context: Match Score: How close is the match?

name: True Positive Investigation
description: Investigation step executed when an AML screening match is confirmed as a true positive. The step identifies the specific list hit (sanctions, PEP, or adverse media), determines the appropriate action pathway, and documents the investigation findings with evidence and approver sign-off.
context: Identify Reason: Which list? What's the designation (sanctions, PEP, adverse media)?

name: True Positive Confirmation Gate
description: A branching decision point that determines whether an AML screening match is confirmed as a true positive. The outcome triggers different investigation and action pathways based on the type of list hit.

name: List Hit Reason Identification
description: Step to identify and document which screening list generated the match and the specific designation assigned (sanctions, PEP, or adverse media). This classification determines the subsequent action pathway.
context: Identify Reason: Which list? What's the designation (sanctions, PEP, adverse media)?

name: Sanctions Hit Decision
description: Decision point that branches when a sanctions list match is confirmed. The path leads to automatic account freeze and escalation to OFSI.
context: Sanctions Hit: Automatic FREEZE + Escalate to OFSI

name: PEP Hit Decision
description: Decision point that branches when a PEP (Politically Exposed Person) list match is confirmed. The path requires enhanced due diligence and escalation to the Compliance Head.
context: PEP Hit: Enhanced due diligence required (escalate to Compliance Head)

name: Adverse Media Hit Decision
description: Decision point that branches when an adverse media match is confirmed. The path leads to risk assessment with potential to proceed under monitoring.
context: Adverse Media: Risk assessment (may proceed with monitoring)

name: Sanctions Action Determination
description: Step to execute automatic account freeze and initiate escalation to OFSI when a sanctions list hit is confirmed as a true positive.
context: Sanctions Hit: Automatic FREEZE + Escalate to OFSI

name: PEP Enhanced Due Diligence Escalation
description: Step to escalate a confirmed PEP match to the Compliance Head and initiate enhanced due diligence procedures.
context: PEP Hit: Enhanced due diligence required (escalate to Compliance Head)

name: Adverse Media Risk Assessment
description: Step to conduct risk assessment when an adverse media match is confirmed. The assessment determines whether the account may proceed with enhanced monitoring or requires further action.
context: Adverse Media: Risk assessment (may proceed with monitoring)

name: Investigation Documentation
description: Step to formally document the true positive investigation findings, including match assessment notes, decision rationale, evidence reviewed, and approver authorization with date.

name: Compliance Head
description: Senior compliance role responsible for escalation and approval of enhanced due diligence procedures when PEP matches are confirmed.

name: OFSI Escalation Authority
description: External regulatory authority (Office of Financial Sanctions Implementation) to which sanctions hits must be escalated and reported.

name: Investigation Approver
description: Role responsible for reviewing, approving, and signing off on the true positive investigation documentation with date and name.

name: Sanctions List Screening
description: AML screening check against sanctions lists that, when confirmed as a true positive, triggers automatic account freeze and OFSI escalation.
context: Sanctions Hit: Automatic FREEZE + Escalate to OFSI

name: PEP List Screening
description: AML screening check against PEP (Politically Exposed Person) lists that, when confirmed as a true positive, requires enhanced due diligence and Compliance Head escalation.
context: PEP Hit: Enhanced due diligence required (escalate to Compliance Head)

name: Adverse Media Screening
description: AML screening check against adverse media sources that, when confirmed as a true positive, requires risk assessment and may proceed with monitoring.
context: Adverse Media: Risk assessment (may proceed with monitoring)

name: Sanctions Compliance Gate
description: Mandatory regulatory compliance checkpoint verifying that confirmed sanctions hits are properly frozen and escalated to OFSI in accordance with financial sanctions regulations.
context: Sanctions Hit: Automatic FREEZE + Escalate to OFSI

name: PEP Compliance Gate
description: Mandatory regulatory compliance checkpoint verifying that confirmed PEP matches trigger enhanced due diligence procedures and appropriate escalation.
context: PEP Hit: Enhanced due diligence required (escalate to Compliance Head)

name: False Positive Resolution
description: A process step executed when a fraud or compliance flag is determined to be a false positive. The step involves documenting the reasoning for the false positive determination, recording it in the system to prevent re-flagging, proceeding with account opening, and archiving the assessment for audit purposes.

name: False Positive Assessment Documenter
description: The role responsible for documenting the reasoning behind a false positive determination, recording it in the system, and archiving the assessment. This role ensures that false positives are properly tracked to prevent unnecessary re-flagging.

name: False Positive Determination Gate
description: A decision point that branches the process based on whether a fraud or compliance alert is determined to be a false positive. If true, the process follows the false positive resolution path; if false, escalation or other remedial action is implied.

name: Account Opening Process
description: An end-to-end account opening workflow that includes fraud and compliance screening steps, with a false positive resolution pathway. The process includes a 2–4 hour timeline for resolving false positive determinations before account activation can proceed.

name: AML Screening Process
description: The process of recording and documenting AML screening results in the Account Management System, including screening reference numbers, customer identification, screening dates, lists searched, and outcomes (Pass/Hit/Under Review). Results are retained for a minimum of 5 years in compliance with AML regulations.

name: System Documentation Recording
description: The step in which AML screening results are formally recorded in system fields including screening reference number, customer ID, screening date/time, lists searched, pass/hit results with match scores, and approval decisions.

name: Result Documentation
description: The step documenting the outcome of AML screening as Pass, Hit, or Under Review, with associated details such as match score, matched name, and list source when applicable.
context: If hit: Match score, matched name, list

name: Review Decision Recording
description: The step recording the decision, approver identity, and resolution date when a screening result has been reviewed and a determination made.
context: If reviewed: Decision, approver, resolution date

name: AMS Storage and Linking
description: The step of storing screening results in the Account Management System, linking records to the customer record, and ensuring accessibility for audit purposes.

name: Screening Result Approver
description: The role responsible for reviewing AML screening results and recording the approval decision, approver identity, and resolution date when a hit or under-review status requires determination.
context: If reviewed: Decision, approver, resolution date

name: AML Screening Result Recording
description: The formal recording of AML screening outcomes including pass/hit status, match scores, matched names, lists searched, and approval decisions, with mandatory retention for 5 years under AML regulations.
context: If hit: Match score, matched name, list

name: AML Screening Compliance Checkpoint
description: The mandatory compliance gate verifying that AML screening has been completed, results recorded, and documentation retained in accordance with AML regulations for a minimum of 5 years.

name: Account Management System
description: The system responsible for storing AML screening results, generating screening reference numbers, linking records to customer profiles, and maintaining audit trails for regulatory compliance.

name: Sanctions Hit Handling Process
description: Immediate response procedure for sanctions hits detected during account screening against OFAC, EU, HMT, and UN sanctions lists. Requires immediate account freeze, escalation to compliance leadership, regulatory notification to OFSI within 24 hours, and SAR filing with NCA. Customer communication is restricted to prevent tipping off.
context: Timeline: Immediate + regulatory notification within 24 hours

name: Account Freeze on Sanctions Hit
description: First action upon detection of a sanctions hit: account is frozen immediately with no transactions permitted. This is a precautionary measure pending compliance review and regulatory notification.

name: Escalation to Compliance Leadership
description: Sanctions hit is escalated immediately to both the Compliance Head and Head of Financial Crime for senior review and decision-making on next steps.
context: Escalate to Compliance Head + Head of Financial Crime

name: OFSI Regulatory Notification
description: Mandatory notification to OFSI (Office of Financial Sanctions Implementation, UK Treasury) within 24 hours when a UK sanctions hit is confirmed. This is a regulatory obligation for UK-based financial institutions.
context: Notify OFSI (UK Treasury) within 24 hours (if UK sanctions hit)

name: Suspicious Activity Report Filing
description: Mandatory filing of a Suspicious Activity Report with the National Crime Agency (NCA) as part of the sanctions hit response procedure. This documents the suspicious activity and regulatory action taken.
context: File Suspicious Activity Report (SAR) with NCA

name: System Documentation of Hold Reason
description: Internal system recording of the reason for account freeze, creating an audit trail and compliance record of the sanctions hit and the action taken.

name: Customer Communication on Account Freeze
description: Generic customer communication informing them that their account has been frozen pending review, without disclosing the AML or sanctions reason to avoid tipping off. If customer questions the freeze, the matter is escalated to a manager.
context: Generic message: "Your account has been frozen pending review"
Escalate to manager if customer questions

name: Sanctions Hit Confirmation Decision
description: Critical decision point determining whether the sanctions hit is a false positive or a confirmed true positive. This decision determines whether the account is unfrozen and the customer relationship continues, or the account remains frozen with potential closure.
context: Hit confirmed as false positive → Unfreeze, apologize, proceed
Hit confirmed as true positive → Remain frozen, potential account closure

name: Compliance Head
description: Senior compliance officer responsible for receiving escalation of sanctions hits and making decisions on account freeze confirmation and regulatory response.
context: Escalate to Compliance Head + Head of Financial Crime

name: Head of Financial Crime
description: Senior financial crime officer responsible for receiving escalation of sanctions hits and determining appropriate regulatory and operational response.
context: Escalate to Compliance Head + Head of Financial Crime

name: Account Manager
description: Manager responsible for handling customer inquiries about account freeze when customer questions the reason for the freeze.
context: Escalate to manager if customer questions

name: Sanctions List Screening Checkpoint
description: Mandatory compliance checkpoint verifying that customer and account details are screened against OFAC, EU, HMT, and UN sanctions lists. A hit at this checkpoint triggers immediate account freeze and regulatory response.

name: Sanctions Screening
description: Screening of customer and account against multiple sanctions lists including OFAC (US), EU sanctions, HMT (UK), and UN sanctions lists. Hits trigger immediate account freeze and regulatory notification.

name: Sanctions Hit Suspicious Activity Report
description: Mandatory Suspicious Activity Report filed with the National Crime Agency (NCA) when a sanctions hit is detected and confirmed. Part of the regulatory response to sanctions violations.
context: File Suspicious Activity Report (SAR) with NCA

name: Account Holder Subject to Sanctions Screening
description: Customer whose account is subject to sanctions screening and who may be matched against OFAC, EU, HMT, or UN sanctions lists. If a hit occurs, the customer is notified generically without disclosure of the sanctions reason.
context: Generic message: "Your account has been frozen pending review"
Do NOT inform customer of reason (tipping off risk)

name: Account Subject to Sanctions Hit
description: Customer account that has been frozen due to a sanctions hit detection. No transactions are permitted on the account pending compliance review and determination of whether the hit is a false positive or true positive.
context: Your account has been frozen pending review

name: PEP Hit Enhanced Due Diligence Process
description: A compliance workflow triggered when a customer matches a Politically Exposed Person (PEP) list during screening. The process requires escalation to the Compliance Head for risk assessment and approval decision, with enhanced monitoring obligations if the application proceeds. Timeline is 1–2 business days.
context: Action: ENHANCED DUE DILIGENCE (Not automatic block)

name: Flag Customer as PEP
description: Initial step in which the customer is formally flagged in the system as a Politically Exposed Person following a positive match on PEP screening.

name: Escalate to Compliance Head for Review
description: The PEP flag is escalated to the Compliance Head for formal review and risk assessment decision.
context: Escalate to Compliance Head for review

name: Assess PEP Risk Category
description: Compliance Head evaluates the nature and degree of PEP exposure by determining whether the customer is a direct PEP, family member, or close associate, and whether they are a foreign or domestic PEP.
context: Assess risk (family member? Close associate? Foreign PEP?)

name: PEP Application Approval Decision
description: Gate decision following risk assessment where the Compliance Head determines whether to proceed with Enhanced Due Diligence or reject the application outright.
decision_question: Should the application proceed with Enhanced Due Diligence or be rejected?
path_yes: Proceed with Enhanced Due Diligence and implement enhanced monitoring requirements
context: Approval decision: Proceed with EDD / Reject application

name: Implement Enhanced Monitoring Requirements
description: Upon approval to proceed, enhanced monitoring obligations are activated on the customer account, including quarterly transaction monitoring and annual review cycles.

name: Verify Beneficial Ownership
description: Enhanced Due Diligence step requiring verification of beneficial ownership structure where applicable, to establish true control and beneficial interest in the customer entity.

name: Collect Source of Funds Documentation
description: Enhanced Due Diligence step requiring the customer to provide documentation evidencing the legitimate source and origin of funds to be held or transacted through the account.

name: Conduct Quarterly Transaction Monitoring
description: Ongoing Enhanced Due Diligence obligation requiring review and monitoring of customer transactions on a quarterly basis to detect suspicious or unusual activity patterns.

name: Conduct Annual Review
description: Ongoing Enhanced Due Diligence obligation requiring an annual comprehensive review of the customer's PEP status, risk profile, and continued suitability for the banking relationship.

name: Document Risk Assessment
description: Formal recording and documentation of the risk assessment findings, decision rationale, and approval outcome in the customer's compliance file.

name: Compliance Head
description: Senior compliance officer responsible for reviewing PEP flags, assessing risk category, making approval/rejection decisions, and overseeing Enhanced Due Diligence implementation.
context: Escalate to Compliance Head for review
Approval decision: Proceed with EDD / Reject application

name: PEP Screening Compliance Checkpoint
description: Mandatory regulatory gate verifying that customer screening against Politically Exposed Person lists has been completed and that appropriate risk assessment and approval controls are in place before account opening or relationship continuation.
regulatory_basis: AML/CFT regulatory requirements for PEP identification and enhanced due diligence
evidence_required: PEP screening result, risk assessment documentation, approval decision, Enhanced Due Diligence completion evidence
context: Action: ENHANCED DUE DILIGENCE (Not automatic block)

name: Enhanced Due Diligence Verification
description: Comprehensive KYC process applied to PEP customers requiring beneficial ownership verification, source of funds documentation, quarterly transaction monitoring, and annual review to mitigate money laundering and sanctions risks.

name: PEP List Screening
description: Sanctions and PEP list screening control that identifies customers matching Politically Exposed Person databases, triggering the Enhanced Due Diligence process for risk assessment and approval.

name: PEP Customer
description: A customer identified as a Politically Exposed Person through screening, subject to Enhanced Due Diligence requirements including beneficial ownership verification, source of funds documentation, and ongoing transaction monitoring.

name: Adverse Media Hit Risk Assessment Process
description: An end-to-end procedure for evaluating adverse media findings against a customer or applicant. The process involves reviewing media details, assessing materiality to the banking relationship, escalating material findings to the Compliance Head, and making a proceed-or-reject decision. Assessment outcomes are documented and inform ongoing monitoring or application rejection.
context: Decision: Proceed with monitoring / Reject application

name: Review Adverse Media Details
description: The initial step in which news and adverse media details are reviewed to establish the factual basis for risk assessment.

name: Assess Materiality of Adverse Media
description: Evaluation of whether the adverse media finding is material and relevant to the banking relationship, determining whether escalation is warranted.

name: Escalate Material Adverse Media to Compliance Head
description: When adverse media is assessed as material, the finding is escalated to the Compliance Head for senior review and decision-making.
context: If material: Escalate to Compliance Head

name: Document Adverse Media Assessment
description: The final step in which the assessment outcome, decision rationale, and supporting evidence are formally recorded for audit and compliance purposes.

name: Adverse Media Proceed or Reject Decision
description: A branching gate where the assessment outcome determines whether the application or relationship proceeds with monitoring or is rejected. Material findings (e.g., confirmed sanctions violations) lead to rejection; immaterial or resolved findings lead to standard monitoring.
context: Decision: Proceed with monitoring / Reject application
PASS: Old fraud accusation (10+ years ago, no conviction) → Proceed with standard monitoring
REJECT: Recent sanctions violation (confirmed) → Reject application

name: Compliance Head
description: Senior compliance officer responsible for reviewing and deciding on material adverse media findings escalated from the initial assessment step.
context: If material: Escalate to Compliance Head
Decision: Proceed with monitoring / Reject application

name: Adverse Media Assessor
description: The role responsible for reviewing adverse media details, assessing materiality, and documenting the initial assessment outcome.

name: Applicant or Customer Subject to Adverse Media Screening
description: The individual or entity whose name or profile has triggered an adverse media hit during screening, and who is subject to the risk assessment and decision process.

name: Adverse Media Compliance Checkpoint
description: A mandatory regulatory gate that verifies whether an applicant or customer has been subject to adverse media findings and whether such findings are material to the banking relationship. The checkpoint determines whether the relationship can proceed or must be rejected.
context: Decision: Proceed with monitoring / Reject application

name: Ongoing Monitoring
description: Post-screening continuous monitoring process for customer accounts, differentiated by risk classification. Includes periodic re-screening of sanctions lists, transaction monitoring (enhanced or automated based on risk level), and manual or automated review of alerts triggered by defined monitoring criteria.

name: High-Risk Customer Quarterly Re-screening
description: Quarterly re-scan of sanctions lists for customers classified as high-risk, as part of ongoing AML monitoring obligations.

name: High-Risk Customer Enhanced Transaction Monitoring
description: Intensive monitoring of transactions on high-risk customer accounts to detect suspicious or unusual activity patterns.

name: High-Risk Customer Unusual Activity Alert Review
description: Manual review of unusual activity alerts generated for high-risk customer accounts as part of enhanced monitoring procedures.

name: High-Risk Customer Annual Comprehensive Risk Review
description: Annual comprehensive reassessment of risk profile for high-risk customers, incorporating findings from ongoing monitoring activities.

name: Standard-Risk Customer Annual Re-screening
description: Annual re-scan of sanctions lists for customers classified as standard-risk, as part of ongoing AML monitoring obligations.

name: Standard-Risk Customer Automated Transaction Monitoring
description: Automated monitoring of transactions on standard-risk customer accounts using predefined rules to identify suspicious patterns.

name: Standard-Risk Customer Alert Review by Automated Rules
description: Automated review and processing of transaction monitoring alerts for standard-risk customers using predefined rule sets.

name: Large Transaction Detection
description: Monitoring trigger activated when a transaction exceeds £50,000, flagging the transaction for enhanced scrutiny and potential alert generation.

name: High-Risk Jurisdiction Transaction Detection
description: Monitoring trigger activated when a transaction is directed to or originates from a high-risk jurisdiction, requiring enhanced review.

name: New Beneficiary or Payee Detection
description: Monitoring trigger activated when a customer initiates a transaction to a new beneficiary or payee not previously recorded on the account.

name: Rapid Transaction Velocity Detection
description: Monitoring trigger activated when multiple transactions occur in a short time period, indicating unusual transaction velocity that may signal suspicious activity.
context: Rapid transaction velocity (multiple in short time)

name: Sanctions List Re-screening Compliance Gate
description: Mandatory compliance gate ensuring periodic re-screening of customer records against current sanctions lists (quarterly for high-risk, annually for standard-risk customers) as required by AML regulations.

name: Ongoing Transaction Monitoring
description: Continuous AML screening of customer transactions post-account opening, differentiated by customer risk classification. Includes both enhanced manual monitoring for high-risk customers and automated rule-based monitoring for standard-risk customers.

name: High-Risk Customer
description: Customer classified as high-risk, subject to enhanced ongoing monitoring including quarterly re-screening, enhanced transaction monitoring, manual alert review, and annual comprehensive risk review.

name: Standard-Risk Customer
description: Customer classified as standard-risk, subject to standard ongoing monitoring including annual re-screening, automated transaction monitoring, and automated alert review.

name: Large Transaction
description: Transaction exceeding £50,000 that triggers monitoring alerts and enhanced scrutiny as part of ongoing AML monitoring procedures.

name: High-Risk Jurisdiction Transaction
description: Transaction directed to or originating from a high-risk jurisdiction, triggering monitoring alerts and enhanced review.

name: Rapid Velocity Transaction
description: Multiple transactions occurring in a short time period on a customer account, triggering monitoring alerts for unusual transaction velocity.
context: Rapid transaction velocity (multiple in short time)

name: Account Opening Process
description: End-to-end account opening workflow that includes mandatory screening checks. The process cannot proceed if the screening system is unavailable and must be delayed until screening is complete.
context: Do NOT proceed with account opening (screening mandatory)
Account opening delayed until screening complete

name: Document Outage Time
description: Initial step in the screening system outage troubleshooting procedure where the time and duration of the system outage is formally recorded.

name: Screening Mandatory Verification
description: Mandatory compliance step that verifies screening has been completed before account opening can proceed. This step blocks account opening if screening is unavailable.
context: Do NOT proceed with account opening (screening mandatory)

name: Escalate to Technology Team
description: Escalation step triggered when the screening system is unavailable, requiring immediate notification and resolution by the Technology team.

name: System Restoration Retry
description: Step to retry the account opening process once the screening system has been restored to operational status.

name: Technology Team
description: Team responsible for resolving screening system outages and restoring system availability to enable account opening to proceed.

name: Account Opening Staff
description: Operations staff responsible for executing account opening steps and managing the workflow when the screening system is unavailable.
context: Do NOT proceed with account opening
Account opening delayed until screening complete

name: Screening System Availability Gate
description: Critical decision point that determines whether the account opening process can proceed. If the screening system is unavailable, the process is blocked and escalated; if available, screening proceeds.
context: Do NOT proceed with account opening (screening mandatory)

name: Screening Compliance Checkpoint
description: Mandatory regulatory compliance gate that must be passed before account opening can be completed. Screening is non-negotiable and blocks the entire process if unavailable.
context: Account opening delayed until screening complete

name: New Account
description: The account being opened through the account opening process, which is subject to mandatory screening requirements before it can be activated.
context: Account opening delayed until screening complete

name: False Positive Management Process
description: A procedure for managing customers who frequently trigger false positive alerts during screening. The process involves documenting previous assessments, updating customer profiles with verified flags, and considering alternative name variants to expedite future screening cycles.
context: If Customer Frequently Hit on Screening
Consider alternative name variant for faster screening

name: Document Previous False Positive Assessments
description: The first step in managing a frequently-screened customer, requiring the recording of all prior false positive determinations in the customer's file for audit and reference purposes.

name: Update Customer Profile with Verified Flag
description: A system update step that marks the customer profile with a 'verified' flag to indicate that previous screening hits have been assessed and cleared as false positives.

name: Re-screen Customer Against Updated Lists
description: A screening step that re-runs the customer against current screening lists, acknowledging that alerts may still trigger due to list updates even after verification.
context: Re-screen may still trigger (due to list updates), but quick resolution

name: Consider Alternative Name Variant for Screening
description: An optimization step that evaluates alternative name variants or spelling variations for the customer to reduce future false positive screening hits and accelerate resolution.
context: Consider alternative name variant for faster screening

name: Screening Operations Team
description: The operational team responsible for executing the false positive management process, including documentation, profile updates, re-screening, and name variant evaluation.
context: Consider alternative name variant for faster screening

name: Customer Screening
description: The ongoing screening process that checks customers against sanctions and watchlists, which may generate false positive alerts that require management and resolution.
context: If Customer Frequently Hit on Screening
Re-screen may still trigger (due to list updates), but quick resolution

name: Frequently Screened Customer
description: A customer who repeatedly triggers screening alerts, requiring special handling through false positive assessment and profile management to distinguish genuine risk from name-matching coincidence.
context: If Customer Frequently Hit on Screening

name: Screening False Positive Verification
description: A mandatory compliance gate that verifies whether a customer's screening alert is a genuine match or a false positive, with documented assessment and profile flagging required before proceeding.

name: Screening Audit Process
description: A periodic quality assurance procedure comprising monthly and annual audit cycles to review screening decisions, verify escalation protocols, document false positives, assess decision timeliness, and confirm list coverage and SAR filing appropriateness.

name: Review Screening Decisions
description: Monthly audit step to review 10 or more screening decisions to assess their accuracy and compliance with established procedures.

name: Verify Hits Escalation
description: Monthly audit step to verify that screening hits have been properly escalated according to established protocols.

name: Document False Positives
description: Monthly audit step to confirm that false positives from screening decisions are properly documented for audit trail and process improvement.

name: Assess Decision Timeliness
description: Monthly audit step to evaluate whether screening decisions are being made within acceptable timeframes.

name: Full Screening Process Review
description: Annual audit step to conduct a comprehensive review of the entire screening process to identify systemic issues and process improvements.

name: Verify List Coverage
description: Annual audit step to confirm that all required screening lists are active and being applied consistently throughout the screening process.

name: Assess Hit Resolution Timeliness
description: Annual audit step to evaluate the timeliness of resolving screening hits from initial detection to final disposition.

name: Assess SAR Filing Appropriateness
description: Annual audit step to review whether Suspicious Activity Reports are being filed appropriately and in accordance with regulatory requirements.

name: Quality Assurance Auditor
description: The role responsible for conducting monthly and annual screening audits, reviewing decisions, verifying escalations, and assessing compliance with screening procedures.

name: Screening List Coverage Compliance Checkpoint
description: A mandatory annual compliance gate to verify that all required screening lists are active and properly maintained as part of the AML screening control framework.

name: SAR Filing Compliance Checkpoint
description: A mandatory annual compliance gate to verify that Suspicious Activity Reports are being filed appropriately and in accordance with regulatory obligations.

name: Screening Hit Detection and Escalation
description: The AML screening process that generates hits requiring escalation, resolution, and documentation as part of the bank's ongoing sanctions and PEP screening obligations.

name: SAR Filing Obligation
description: The regulatory obligation to file Suspicious Activity Reports, subject to annual audit review to ensure appropriateness and timeliness of filings.

name: AML Policy
description: Detailed AML policy document that defines requirements for anti-money laundering screening and compliance obligations across banking operations.

name: KYC Verification Process
description: Know Your Customer verification procedure that precedes AML screening in the account opening workflow. Establishes customer identity and address verification requirements.

name: Account Opening Process
description: End-to-end account opening procedure that includes AML screening as Step 5. Defines the workflow for establishing new customer accounts with all required compliance checks.

name: AML Screening
description: Anti-money laundering screening obligation executed as Step 5 in the account opening process. Includes sanctions and PEP list checks as part of compliance verification.

name: KYC Verification
description: Know Your Customer verification process that precedes AML screening in the account opening workflow. Establishes baseline customer identity and address verification.

name: Business Ontology
description: Reference document defining customer and AML screening entities used across banking operations and compliance procedures.

name: Head of Financial Crime
description: Senior role responsible for authoring and maintaining financial crime operational procedures, including AML screening, hit handling, and ongoing monitoring protocols.
context: Added hit handling procedures, ongoing monitoring | Head of Financial Crime
Initial SOP | Head of Financial Crime

name: Head of Financial Crime
description: Senior role responsible for financial crime oversight and approval of operational procedures. Holds sign-off authority on compliance and operational documents.
context: Approved by: Head of Financial Crime — Date: 2026-01-15

name: Head of Compliance
description: Senior compliance role responsible for regulatory oversight and approval of operational procedures. Holds sign-off authority on compliance matters.
